newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI sees A$150 mln sales for drugs unit.
newsitem.headline: ICI sees A$150 mln sales for drugs unit.

text.p: MELBOURNE, June 25 (Reuter) ICI Australia Ltd said on Wednesday its pharmaceuticals business, under sale negotiations, would take in sales revenue of about A$150 million in the year to September 30, 1998.
The drugs business was the major part of the Advanced Sciences division which had a gross profit margin of around 14 percent, ICI Australia Managing Director Philip Weickhardt told reporters.
ICI Australia announced last Friday it was negotiating with British pharmaceuticals group Zeneca Plc for the sale of ICI Australia's pharmaceuticals business.
Under a four-year-old agreement between the two companies, Zeneca argues it has a right to buy the business.
Weickhardt rejected criticism that ICI Australia failed to disclose the impact of a sale of the company's pharmaceuticals business on earnings per share.
Earlier, at a shareholders' meeting on the buy-back proposal, concern was voiced over an independent report showing the full buy-back would raise earnings per share by two percent.
The report, by consultancy Grant Samuel and Associates, makes no adjustment for a sale of the pharmaceuticals business in calculating the impact on earnings per share.
Weickhardt said the report was prepared well before ICI Australia agreed with Zeneca on Friday to negotiate a sale.
"The Grant Samuel report and the offering document contain very full disclosures by the company," he told reporters after the meeting aproved the buy-back on a show of hands.
